questions.question: Describe solids, liquids and gases in terms of the Kinetic Molecular Theory, referring to the arrangement of the particles, their motion, the forces between them, and the resulting bulk properties.
questions.expected_answer: In a solid the particles are closely packed in a fixed, regular lattice and vibrate about fixed positions; the forces of attraction are strong and the particles' kinetic energy is too small to overcome them, giving a fixed shape, a fixed volume, high density and almost no compressibility. In a liquid the particles are still close together but irregularly arranged and able to slide past one another; the forces are still significant but the kinetic energy is now enough to break fixed positions, giving a fixed volume, no fixed shape, and still very little compressibility. In a gas the particles are far apart and move rapidly and randomly in straight lines between collisions; the forces between them are negligible, giving no fixed shape, no fixed volume, low density and easy compression because most of the volume is empty space. Which state a substance occupies is decided by the contest between the particles' kinetic energy and the forces of attraction between them.

questions.question: A 2 kg block of ice at −20 °C is heated at a steady rate until it is steam above 100 °C. Sketch the shape of the temperature-time graph in words, and explain why the temperature stays constant during the two plateaus even though heating continues.
questions.expected_answer: The graph rises from −20 °C to 0 °C (solid ice warming), runs horizontally at 0 °C (melting), rises from 0 °C to 100 °C (liquid water warming), runs horizontally for a longer stretch at 100 °C (boiling), and then rises again above 100 °C (steam warming). During the rising sections the supplied energy increases the average kinetic energy of the particles, so the temperature climbs. During the plateaus the supplied energy is used to overcome the forces of attraction between the particles — it increases their potential energy by separating them, not their kinetic energy — so the thermometer does not move while any of the old state remains. The boiling plateau is longer than the melting plateau because separating liquid particles completely into a gas takes far more energy than merely loosening a lattice into a liquid.

questions.question: Name the six changes of state with their directions, classify each as endothermic or exothermic, and explain the difference between evaporation and boiling.
questions.expected_answer: Melting is solid to liquid, freezing (solidification) is liquid to solid, evaporation and boiling are liquid to gas, condensation is gas to liquid, sublimation is solid straight to gas (as with dry ice), and deposition is gas straight to solid (as when frost forms on Highveld grass). Melting, evaporation and sublimation move the substance towards weaker forces and more freedom, so all three absorb energy and are endothermic; freezing, condensation and deposition move towards stronger holding, so all three release energy and are exothermic. Evaporation occurs at any temperature, only at the surface of the liquid, and only for particles with above-average kinetic energy escaping upwards — which is why the remaining liquid cools. Boiling occurs only at the boiling point, throughout the whole liquid, with bubbles of vapour forming inside it, and it happens when the liquid's vapour pressure equals the surrounding atmospheric pressure.
